# Analysis strategy

We test the hypothesis that bias toward false alarms when detecting contagious individuals positively predicts prejudice toward groups with a superficial anomaly in appearance. Prejudice is measured with separate "feeling thermometers" for 12 different targets, of which we consider four to be most important.

Our main analysis is a regression model of prejudice (P) on participant sex (S) and decision criterion (C) in the sickness detection task. P is measured on a 0-1 visual analogue scale, and we assume it is normally distributed conditional on the model. S is treated as a binary factor (male / female) and entered into the regression with contrast codes (f: -0.5, m: 0.5). C is a SDT metric that theoretically varies without bound but is typically in the -3 to 3 range. For all participants j we model prejudice as

$$
P_j \sim \text{Normal}
\left(\beta_0 + \beta_1S_j + \beta_2C_j, \sigma^2 \right)
$$

We will estimate this regression separately for all 12 feeling thermometers.

## Sample size planning

Here we examine statistical power for a single prejudice thermometer assuming the following:

- Minimum effect size of interest is r = 0.1 between C and P
- P and S correlate at r = 0.2 (conservative estimate from prior data)
- S and C correlate at r = 0.2 (conservative assumption)

We first define a function that simulates data from this multivariate normal distribution, and then calculates the critical regression coefficient's p-value.

```{r}
# Functions to simulate data and calculate coefficient p-value
simulate <- function(
    n = 30, 
    cor_prejudice_sex = 0, 
    cor_prejudice_criterion = 0, 
    cor_sex_criterion = 0
) {
  
  # Simulate from multivariate normal distribution
  latent <- rnorm_multi(
    n = n, 
    mu = c(0, 0, 0),
    sd = c(1, 1, 1),
    r = c(cor_prejudice_sex, cor_prejudice_criterion, cor_sex_criterion), 
    varnames = c("prejudice", "sex", "criterion"),
    empirical = FALSE
  )
  
  # Categorize latent terms
  observed <- latent |> 
    mutate(
      sex = norm2binom(x = sex, size = 1, prob = pnorm(sex)),
      sex = factor(sex, levels = 0:1, labels = c("Female", "Male"))
    )
  
  contrasts(observed$sex) <- c(-0.5, 0.5)
  
  # Fit model
  fit <- lm(prejudice ~ sex + criterion, data = observed)
  # Calculate one-sided pvalue from tvalue
  tvalue <- summary(fit)$coefficients["criterion", "t value"]
  pvalue <- pt(tvalue, fit$df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  pvalue
}
```

We then run this over a grid of assumptions

```{r}
# Find power for a set of parameters
path <- "cache/sim-1.rds"
if (!file.exists(path)) {
  library(furrr)
  plan(multisession, workers = 8)
  
  sim <- crossing(
    n = seq(500, 2000, by = 100),
    cor_prejudice_sex = c(0, 0.1, 0.2),
    cor_prejudice_criterion = 0.1,
    cor_sex_criterion = c(0, 0.1, 0.2),
    i = 1:1000
  ) |> 
    mutate(
      simulation = future_pmap_dbl(
        list(n, cor_prejudice_sex, cor_prejudice_criterion, cor_sex_criterion), 
        ~simulate(
          n=..1, 
          cor_prejudice_sex=..2, 
          cor_prejudice_criterion=..3, 
          cor_sex_criterion=..4
        )
      )
    )
  sim <- sim |>   
    summarise(
      simulation = mean(simulation <= 0.05),
      .by = c(n, cor_prejudice_sex, cor_prejudice_criterion, cor_sex_criterion)
    )
  saveRDS(sim, path)
} else {sim <- readRDS(path)}
```

Calculate simple power

```{r}
sim <- sim |> 
  mutate(
    calculation = map2_dbl(
      n, cor_prejudice_criterion, 
      ~pwr.r.test(n=..1, r=..2, alternative = "greater")$power
    )
  )
```

And then plot the results

```{r}
#| label: fig-power
#| fig-cap: Probability of rejecting the null hypothesis over a range of sample sizes and correlations. Theoretical power refers to power where the variables do not correlate; actual power to where the variables do correlate.

sim |> 
  pivot_longer(c(simulation, calculation)) |> 
  mutate(
    `Cor(S, C)` = number(cor_sex_criterion, .01),
    `Cor(S, P)` = number(cor_prejudice_sex, .01)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(n, value, col = name)) +
  scale_color_brewer(
    "Power",
    palette = "Set1",
    breaks = c("calculation", "simulation"),
    labels = c("Theoretical\n(analytic)", "Actual\n(simulated)")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Power",
    labels = ~percent(.)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    "Number of participants",
    breaks = extended_breaks()
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.9, linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(
    `Cor(S, C)` ~ `Cor(S, P)`, 
    labeller = label_both
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1))
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(margin = unit(rep(4, 4), "pt")),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

The minimum number of participants needed here to get 90% power is about `r min(sim$n[sim$simulation > 0.9 & sim$cor_prejudice_sex == 0.2 & sim$cor_sex_criterion == 0.2])`.

# Results

```{r}
#| label: data-qualtrics-wrangle
#| output: false

# Load data with good names
# Qualtrics SPSS output is most informative and therefore used here
dat <- read_spss(Sys.getenv("PATH_QUALTRICS_SPSS")) |>
  clean_names() |> 
  rename(pid = response_id) |> 
  filter(consent == 1)

# Count exclusions
s <- list()
s$total_before_exclusions <- nrow(dat)
s$not_english <- nrow(dat[dat$language != 1, ])
s$not_us <- nrow(dat[dat$residence != 1, ])
s$not_18 <- nrow(dat[dat$age < 18, ])
s$not_attention <- nrow(dat[dat$attention_check != 3, ])

# Apply exclusion criteria
dat <- dat |>
  filter(
    consent == 1,
    language == 1,
    residence == 1,
    age >= 18,
    # attention_check == 4
  )
s$total_after_exclusions <- nrow(dat)

# Remove unnecessary variables
dat <- dat |> 
  select(
    -c(start_date:q50, consent, language, residence, attention_check), 
    pid
  )

# Create SDT metrics

## Load mapping between stimulus and target type from file
mapping <- map(
  c("sick_v1", "sick_v2", "criminal"), 
  ~read_excel("data-raw/mapping.xlsx", sheet = .x) |> 
    mutate(task = .x, .before = 1)
) |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  clean_names()

## Wrangle data to appropriate format for subsequent calculations
sdt <- dat |> 
  select(pid, contains("_sick_"), contains("criminal")) |>
  pivot_longer(-pid, values_to = "response") |> 
  # This drops all items with missing response
  # including those in task (v1, v2) that participant was not assigned to
  drop_na(response) |> 
  separate(name, c("image_url", "task"), sep = "_", extra = "merge") |> 
  # Match item names here to "Image URL"s in mapping.xlsx
  mutate(image_url = str_c("URL ", str_remove(image_url, "a"))) |> 
  # Join to URL-target mapping data
  left_join(mapping) |> 
  # Task v1 / v2 no longer needed
  mutate(task = str_remove(task, "_v[0-9]"))

## Take SDT task data out of main data
dat <- dat |> 
  select(-contains("_sick_"), -contains("criminal"))

## Exclude individuals with 5 or more missing disease task responses
sdt <- sdt |> 
  filter(task == "sick") |> 
  count(pid, task) |> 
  filter(n >= 9) |> 
  distinct(pid) |> 
  left_join(sdt)

## Recode and harmonize response and target values
## Task is to detect sick or criminal, code responses to No / Yes
sdt <- sdt |> 
  mutate(
    response = factor(response, levels = c(2, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    target = factor(
      condition_type_of_target %in% c("sick", "criminal"),
      levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
      labels = c("No", "Yes")
    )
  )
## Verify calculation here
count(sdt, condition_type_of_target, target)
sdt <- select(sdt, -condition_type_of_target)

## Calculate SDT metrics (1: Trial outcome)
sdt <- sdt |> 
  mutate(
    type = "hit",
    type = ifelse(target == "Yes" & response == "No", "miss", type),
    type = ifelse(target == "No" & response == "No", "cr", type),
    type = ifelse(target == "No" & response == "Yes", "fa", type)
  )
count(sdt, target, response, type)

## Calculate SDT metrics (2: z scores and parameters)
sdt <- sdt |> 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    .by = c(pid, task, type)
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = n) |> 
  mutate(
    zhr = qnorm(hit / (hit + miss)),
    zfa = qnorm(fa / (fa + cr)),
    dprime = zhr - zfa,
    crit = -(zhr + zfa) / 2
  )

# Scale scores; lines indicate "clusters" 1 - 4
groups <- c(
  "obese", "elder", "limbs", "mark", 
  "tb", "prison", 
  "gay", "lesb", "home", "addict", "immig", 
  "polit", "lawyer"
)

## Rescale all scale items
scl <- dat |> 
  select(pid, obese1:pds7) |> 
  mutate(
    # Rescale all variables from 1-7 to 0-1
    across(-pid, ~(.x - 1) / 6),
    # Reverse code positive items group prejudice (1, 2, 4, 5)
    across(
      unlist(map(groups, ~paste0(.x, c(1, 2, 4, 5)))),
      ~1 - .x
    )
  )

## Calculate means over items
scl <- scl |> 
  pivot_longer(-pid) |> 
  separate(name, c("scale", "item"), sep = -1) |> 
  summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(pid, scale)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = scale, values_from = value)

## Take out scales from main data
dat <- dat |> 
  select(-c(obese1:pds7))

# Join tables 
dat <- sdt |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = task, values_from = cr:crit) |> 
  left_join(scl, by = "pid") |> 
  left_join(dat, by = "pid")

# Code remaining variables
dat <- dat |> 
  mutate(gender = as_factor(gender))
# We were going to code female: -0.5, male 0.5 to center on grand mean,
# but data has four gender categories so we use the equivalent "ANOVA" coding
# to center on the grand mean instead
library(faux)
dat$gender <- contr_code_anova(dat$gender)

## Group membership
dat_membership <- select(dat, starts_with("member"))
dat <- select(dat, -starts_with("member"))
names(dat_membership) <- paste0("m_", groups)
# Recode responses Yes: 1, No (and everything else) (0)
dat_membership <- dat_membership |> 
  mutate(
    across(everything(), ~ifelse(.x==1, 1, NaN) |> replace_na(0))
  )
dat <- bind_cols(dat, dat_membership)
rm(dat_membership)

# Gender breakdown
genders <- dat |> 
  count(gender) |> 
  mutate(gender = fct_na_value_to_level(gender, "Missing")) |> 
  arrange(desc(n)) |> 
  mutate(gender = str_glue("{gender}: {n}")) |> 
  pull(gender) |> 
  str_to_sentence()
```

## Descriptive results

After excluding `{r} s$total_before_exclusions - s$total_after_exclusions` individuals who did not satisfy the inclusion criteria, the final sample consisted of `{r} s$total_after_exclusions` individuals whose median age was `{r} number(median(dat$age))` years (range: [`{r} paste(range(dat$age), collapse = ", ")`]), with the following self-reported gender breakdown `{r} paste0(genders, collapse = ", ")`. We summarize our key variables in @tbl-descriptives, and their correlations in @tbl-descriptives-cor.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptives
#| tbl-cap: Descriptives of key variables.

tbl_sum <- dat |> 
  select(
    crit_sick, crit_criminal,
    all_of(groups), pds, age
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable") 

tbl_sum |>
  zap_labels() |> 
  summarise(
    m = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    s = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = Variable
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~number(.x, .01)),
    `Mean (SD)` = str_glue("{m} ({s})"),
    Range = str_glue("[{min}, {max}]")
  ) |> 
  select(Variable, `Mean (SD)`, Range) |> 
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptives-cor
#| tbl-cap: Correlation matrix of key variables.

dat |> 
  select(
    crit_sick, crit_criminal,
    all_of(groups), pds, age
  ) |> 
  correlate() |> 
  shave() |> 
  fashion() |> 
  kable()
```

## Hypothesis tests

We then turned to our main hypothesis test (H1): We regressed all thirteen groups' prejudice scores on decision criteria from the sickness detection task, and report the key regression parameters in @tbl-h1.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h1
#| tbl-cap: Results from regressions of prejudice scores on contagion task decision criteria.

# Do all regressions
tbl_fit <- tibble(
  group = groups,
  # Analysis 1
  fit_base = map(
    group, 
    ~lm(str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick + gender"), data = dat)
  ),
  fit_sex = map(
    group, 
    ~lm(str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick * gender"), data = dat)
  ),
  # Analysis 2
  # Models without people not members in that category
  fit_mem = map(
    group,
    ~lm(
      str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick + gender"), 
      data = filter(dat, get(paste0("m_", .x)) != 1)
    )
  ),
  fit_mem_sex = map(
    group,
    ~lm(
      str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick * gender"), 
      data = filter(dat, get(paste0("m_", .x)) != 1)
    )
  ),
  # Analysis 3
  # Adjusting for Ccriminal
  fit_crim = map(
    group, 
    ~lm(str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick + gender + crit_criminal"), data = dat)
  ),
  fit_crim_sex = map(
    group, 
    ~lm(str_glue("{.x} ~ crit_sick * gender + crit_criminal"), data = dat)
  ),
)
```

Everything below here will change as data comes in (model selection etc.) For example...

```{r}

# Summarise regressions
tbl_hyp <- tbl_fit |> 
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "model") |> 
  mutate(model = str_remove(model, "fit_")) |> 
  mutate(
    sum = map(
      value, 
      ~tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) |> 
        # One-sided p smaller than zero is (one minus) p / 2
        mutate(
          p.smaller = ifelse(
            sign(statistic) == -1, 
            p.value / 2, 
            1 - p.value / 2)
        )
    )
  ) |> 
  select(-value) |> 
  unnest(sum)

# Or slopes by sex
avg_slopes(tbl_fit$fit_sex[[1]], variables = "crit_sick", by = "gender")

# Some kind of table
tbl_hyp |> 
  filter(model == "base", term == "crit_sick") |> 
  mutate(
    across(c(where(is.numeric), -p.smaller), ~number(.x, .01)),
    Estimate = str_glue("{estimate} ({std.error}) [{conf.low}, {conf.high}]"),
    p.smaller = pvalue(p.smaller, add_p = TRUE)
  ) |> 
  select(group, term, Estimate, p.smaller) |> 
  kable()
```
